name: Example: Finding the Minimum Value Given a Canonical Form on the Unit Sphere
problem: Find the minimum value of $Q(\mathbf{x})=5x_1^2 - 4x_2^2 - 6x_3^2$ given that $\| \mathbf{x} \| =1.$
worked_solution:
First, notice that $x_1^2 \geq 0$ and $x_2^2 \geq 0.$ So, we have that

$$
5x_1^2 \geq -6x_1^2, \qquad -4x_2^2 \geq -6x_2^2.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =5{x}_{1}^{2}-4{x}_{2}^{2}-6{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & \ge -6{x}_{1}^{2}-6{x}_{2}^{2}-6{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & =-6({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, recall that $\| \mathbf{x} \| = 1$ is equivalent to $x_1^2 + x_2^2 + x_3^2 =1.$ So, 

$$
\begin{aligned}-6({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2})=-6(1)=-6.\end{aligned}
$$

and, in turn, $Q(\mathbf{x}) \geq -6.$

So, the value of $Q(\mathbf{x})$ can be no smaller than $-6.$ But before we conclude that $-6$ is the minimum, we need to find a vector such that $Q(\mathbf{x}) = -6.$

Notice that when ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14070559/assets/d509eb79bc8d9a96b60922166e49d0225eac7a99d2614859c31af15199d4d47c.png) we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =5{x}_{1}^{2}-4{x}_{2}^{2}-6{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & =5(0)^{2}-4(0)^{2}-6(1)^{2} \\  & =-6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, given that $\| \mathbf{x} \| =1,$ the minimum value of $Q(\mathbf{x})$ is equal to $-6.$
